newsitem.title: UK: TUC SAYS UK RATE RISE WILL COST JOBS.
newsitem.headline: TUC SAYS UK RATE RISE WILL COST JOBS.

text.p: Britain's Trades Union Congress said today's rise in official interest rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 would put jobs at risk.
"The latest interest rate rise will put jobs at risk by keeping the pound high and slowing the economy next year," TUC deputy general secretary Brendan Barber said in a statement.
He said the consumer "windfalls" from building society flotations this year were a one-off factor which did not pose a long-term threat to the government's 2.5 percent inflation target.
"Higher interest rates will do nothing to encourage industry to invest in skills and new capacity which are the real barriers to continued expansion in 1998 and beyond," Barber added.
